items.title: Match time clues and forms
items.instructions: Match each time clue to the sentence that fits it.

payload.explanation: Every Saturday signals a routine; last Saturday signals a completed past action.

items.title: Order a request exchange
items.instructions: Put the turns in a logical conversational order.

segments.text: Could you help me write my address?

payload.explanation: The request comes first, then the offer to help, then the address.

items.title: Correct the past form
items.instructions: Fix the verb in this sentence about yesterday.

payload.erroneous_sentence: Yesterday, Linh run to the station.
payload.corrected_sentence: Yesterday, Linh ran to the station.
payload.explanation: A completed event yesterday requires ran.

items.title: Ask for form-filling help
items.instructions: Make a request and provide a made-up address when your partner asks.

payload.communicative_goal: Ask someone to write a fictional address on a form.
constraints: Give a clearly fictional street address.
payload.expected_output: A request, a relevant response, and a fictional address.

rubric.criterion: The request is polite and fits the situation.
The speaker supplies the information needed.

items.title: Write routine and past action
items.instructions: Write two linked sentences contrasting a routine with one event yesterday.

payload.communicative_goal: Contrast habitual run with past ran.
constraints: Include a routine time phrase and yesterday.
payload.expected_output: One present-simple routine and one completed past action.

rubric.criterion: Run and ran agree with their time references.
The two sentences form a clear contrast.
